The Bucharest Tribunal approved the airline’s second application to open insolvency proceedings after rejecting an earlier request on October 14 because of procedural deficiencies. Romanian media reported that the court appointed a consortium of insolvency administrators to oversee the process. The ruling represents a significant new development for AnimaWings, which stopped operating flights at the beginning of October following aircraft availability problems and mounting financial pressure. The carrier’s latest passenger advisory continues to list November 15 as the final day of its current suspension, without guaranteeing a restart on November 16. The airline first applied for insolvency protection on September 30, seeking a legal framework to restructure its debts and continue operating. However, the Bucharest Tribunal rejected that initial application on October 14 because the required procedural documentation had not been completed. Romanian reporting subsequently confirmed that AnimaWings filed a second application on October 20. On October 28, the court approved the new request, according to HotNews.ro, citing aviation-industry reporting and the tribunal’s decision. The appointed judicial administrator is a consortium involving CITR Filiala București, Infinexa Restructuring and Popescu & Asociații Insolvency. Insolvency proceedings provide a framework for addressing creditors and exploring restructuring. They do not, by themselves, establish that the airline has been permanently liquidated. Why AnimaWings Stopped Flying AnimaWings has attributed its operational difficulties partly to repeated technical problems affecting aircraft availability. In September, the carrier announced the withdrawal of six Airbus A220-300 aircraft from operations, severely reducing its available fleet. The technical problems were followed by disruption to commercial operations and growing financial pressures. The airline suspended scheduled flights from early October, initially expecting to resume service later that month. However, the planned restart was postponed as the company pursued legal and operational solutions. Romanian reports identify creditors including banks, airport operators, air traffic management providers and businesses supplying aviation services. What Happens to Passengers With AnimaWings Tickets? Passengers holding reservations through November 15 should expect their flights to be affected by the suspension. According to AnimaWings’ latest published advisory, cancelled services are being processed progressively through its reservation system. The airline says passengers will receive notifications through the email addresses connected to their bookings, including information about available options. Travelers should preserve their booking confirmations, payment records and cancellation notices. Passengers may have rights to refunds or alternative transport under applicable European passenger-protection rules, although the practical handling of claims can become more complicated when an airline enters insolvency. Those who paid by card may also wish to contact their payment provider about available dispute procedures if a refund is not received. Specific entitlements depend on the booking, cancellation circumstances and applicable consumer-protection rules. Will AnimaWings Resume Flights on November 16? The airline’s official advisory continues to state that flights are suspended through November 15, 2026, inclusive. That does not amount to confirmation that the carrier will resume scheduled operations the following day. The court’s approval of insolvency proceedings creates a new legal framework, but future flight operations remain dependent on financial, operational and regulatory developments. Travelers with bookings after November 15 should check directly with the airline before making non-refundable accommodation or transport arrangements. Further passenger information is available through the official AnimaWings advisory .
